deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. Gauss writes the lemniscatic sine as a quotient sl z = P(z)/Q(z) of two entire functions (header: 'Lemnisk. Zähler und Nenner Sin l[emn]', i.e. numerator and denominator of the lemniscatic sine). In modern terms P(z) is the Weierstrass sigma function sigma(z; g2=4, g3=0), whose period lattice is varpi*Z[i]. This is because sl^2 = 1/wp(z;4,0). Q(z) is the associated function sigma_2 for the root e=0, so Q^2 = P^2*wp.

(1) Top line, copied from the previous page, which computed Q. A crossed-out start is followed by
Qz = 1 + 2 z^4/4! - 4 z^8/8! + 408 z^12/12! + 13584 z^16/16! - 838368 z^20/20!.
I checked the first four coefficients. (I checked them through sl = z - z^5/10 + z^9/120 - 11z^13/15600 + 211z^17/3536000 and the relation P = Q*sl, which gives 13584 to rounding.) The z^20 term is left for the CAS.

(2) The left column under 'p' (i.e. for P) is headed S.1. Here S.k = sum over one representative w of each associate class of nonzero zeros of sl (the lattice varpi*Z[i]) of w^(-4k). Equivalently S.k = G_{4k}/4, a quarter of the Eisenstein sum. Gauss lists them as decimal-denominator values and factored:
- S.1 = 1/60 = 1/(2^2*3*5)
- S.2 = 1/2100 = 1/(2^2*3*5^2*7)
- S.3 = 1/(65*1650) = 1/107250 = 1/(2*3*5^3*11*13)
- S.4 = 1/(2^2*3^2*5^4*13*17) = 1/4972500
- S.5 = 1/(2*3^2*5^5*13*17*19)
I verified all five from the wp recursion c_n = 3/((2n+1)(n-3)) * sum c_m c_{n-m}, using c2 = 1/5 and G_{2n} = c_n/(2n-1).

The product P(z) = z * prod_classes (1 - z^4/w^4) gives log(P/z) = -sum_k S.k z^{4k}/k. Hence, writing P/z = sum a_n w^n with w = z^4, Newton's identity gives
n*a_n = -sum_{k=1..n} S.k * a_{n-k}.

(3) Middle column: the resulting coefficients of P/z, read bottom-up:
- a0 = 1
- a1 = -1/(2^2*3*5) = -1/60
- a2 = -1/(2^5*3^2*5*7) = -1/10080
- a3 = +23/(2^7*3^4*5^2*7*11*13) = 552/13!
- a4 = +107/(2^11*3^5*5^3*7^2*11*13*17) = 5136/17!
- a5, written at the top: -851/(2^13*3^6*5^4*7^2*11*13*17*19)
The earlier coefficients agree with P = z - 2z^5/5! - 36z^9/9! + 552z^13/13! + 5136z^17/17! on the next page.

(4) Lower part: computation of a5. The five products are:
- S1*a4 = 107/(2^13 3^6 5^4 7^2 11 13 17)
- S2*a3 = 23/(2^9 3^5 5^4 7^2 11 13)
- S3*a2 = -1/(2^6 3^3 5^4 7 11 13)
- S4*a1 = -1/(2^4 3^3 5^5 13 17)
- S5 = +1/(2 3^2 5^5 13 17 19)
Gauss pairs them:
- First two: 107 + 23*16*3*17 = 107 + 18768 = 18875. This gives 18875/(2^13 3^6 5^4 7^2 11 13 17) = 3775/(2^13 3^6 5^3 7^2 11 13 17).
- Last two: -19 + 24 = 5. This gives +1/(2^4 3^3 5^4 13 17 19).
- That result with S3*a2: -323 + 4*7*11 = -15. This gives -15/(2^6 3^3 5^4 7 11 13 17 19) = -1/(2^6 3^2 5^3 7 11 13 17 19).
- Final sum: 3775*19 = 71725 and 2^7*3^4*7 = 128*81*7 = 72576. So the total is (71725 - 72576)/(2^13 3^6 5^3 7^2 11 13 17 19) = -851/(...).
Dividing by 5 gives the entry 851/(... 5^4 ...) at the top.

(5) Side computations.
- The dot tables for 2, 3, 5, ..., 19 count prime exponents in 20!. The scratch products (128*81*7, 1024, 10368, 72576; 259459200 = 13*19958400, 19958400 = 11*1814400, 1814400 = 7*259200, 259200 = 32*8100) are factorizations of 12! and 13! style denominators.
- The entries 1440, 851, 3404, 32*9*5, 122544 convert the z^21 coefficient to an integer numerator (851*144 = 122544). '8/(12*19)' and 36*143, 286, 1716, 5148 prepare the next page.
- Left column '60, 45+, 47+, 47+, 235': these are k-th roots of 1/S.k. They are 60, sqrt(2100) = 45.8, cbrt(107250) = 47.5, and 4972500^(1/4) (via sqrt = 2230, then sqrt) = 47.2. The scratch 47^2 = 2209 and 47^3 = 103823 check the cube root. They converge to varpi^4 = 47.27, since S.k ~ varpi^(-4k) from the four nearest zeros +-varpi, +-i*varpi.
- Likewise S.4/S.5 = 47.5 ('47,5'). Then sqrt(47.5) = 6.8922, 6.8922/4 = 1.723 and sqrt(1.723) = 1.312, so 47.5^(1/4) = 2*1.3126 = 2.625, approximately varpi = 2.622.
This is a numerical plausibility check of the lattice sums against the lemniscate constant.
errors: Sign of the z^21 coefficient: by Gauss's own recursion a5 = -(1/5)(S1a4+S2a3+S3a2+S4a1+S5) = -(1/5)(-851/(2^13 3^6 5^3 ...)) = +851/(2^13 3^6 5^4 7^2 11 13 17 19). Gauss writes -851 at the top, and -122544 on the next page. The correct term is +5146848 z^21/21! (5146848 = 32*160839, matching Weierstrass's a_{5,0} = 160839 with g2/2 = 2). This is a sign slip.

Numerator 122544 = 851*144 does not match either normalisation of 851/(2^13 3^6 5^4 7^2 11 13 17 19). 20!/denominator = 288 gives 245088/20!, and 21!/denominator = 6048 gives 5146848/21!. Gauss's numerator is off by a factor of 2 (for 20!) or 42 (for 21!); the purpose of 1440 = 32*9*5 is unclear.
All other arithmetic on the page checks: S.1 to S.5, a1 to a4, 18875, -19+24 = 5, -323+308 = -15, and 71725 - 72576 = -851.
Minor: the first value of the root column (60) is crude because of the alternating contribution of the classes (1+i)varpi with w^4 = -4 varpi^4. This is not an error, only a slow approximation.

results.what: Power series of the numerator P and denominator Q of the lemniscatic sine (sl = P/Q), up to z^21.
results.modern_name: Taylor coefficients of the Weierstrass sigma function sigma(z;4,0) and of the co-sigma function sigma_2 for the lemniscatic lattice
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass, Werke III, 1876); general sigma recursion Weierstrass 1882

results.what: The power sums S.k = sum over associate classes of zeros w of w^(-4k), evaluated exactly as rationals for k=1..5: 1/60, 1/2100, 1/107250, 1/4972500, 1/(2*3^2*5^5*13*17*19).
results.modern_name: Eisenstein series G_{4k} of the Gaussian lattice varpi*Z[i]; S.k = 2^(4k-2) H_{4k}/(4k)! with Hurwitz numbers H4=1/10, H8=3/10, H12=567/130, H16=43659/170, H20=392931/10
results.usually_credited_to: Hurwitz (1899) for the systematic Hurwitz numbers

results.what: Passing from the product P = z*prod(1 - z^4/w^4) to the Taylor series via log P = log z - sum S.k z^{4k}/k and Newton's recursion.
results.modern_name: Newton's identities / exponential of log-derivative (Weierstrass product to Taylor series)
results.usually_credited_to: Newton/Euler (method); applied to sigma by Weierstrass

results.what: Numerical check that (1/S.k)^(1/k) and S.4/S.5 approach varpi^4 = 47.27, recovering varpi = 2.62.
results.modern_name: Asymptotics of lattice Eisenstein sums dominated by shortest vectors

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's P/Q expansions of the lemniscatic functions are known from Werke III. What is less commonly highlighted is that he obtained them here via exact rational values of the lemniscatic lattice power sums, equivalent to the Hurwitz numbers H4 to H20 (Hurwitz 1899), and checked them numerically against varpi. That is a notable unpublished detail, though it is close in spirit to Gauss's known product formulas. The page also has a sign slip in the last coefficient.

transcription_corrections: '49725007 2230' should read '4972500 ±2230': 4972500 = 1/S.4 and sqrt(4972500) is about 2230, the first step toward its 4th root.
'107250 47' is '107250, cube root about 47' (47^3 = 103823 is computed below it).
In the top entry '-851/(2^13 3^6 5^4 ...)', the exponent of 5 appears to be written over (3 changed to 4).
The five fractions in the S.1 column are S.1 ... S.5 (the label applies to the whole column).
